newsitem.title: SWEDEN: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON TO LEARN SOON IF HE CAN COMPETE IN ATHENS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON TO LEARN SOON IF HE CAN COMPETE IN ATHENS.

text.p: Double Olympic champion Michael Johnson will learn in the next few days if he can compete at the Athens world championships next month, athletics sources said on Tuesday.
Johnson did not compete at the U.S. trials because of injury and was not accordingly able to qualify for the American team.
Under the U.S. system only the first three in each event qualify for Olympic Games or world championships.
The International Amateur Athletic Federation is considering whether or not to issue wild cards to defending world champions, who include Johnson and his fellow Americans Gail Devers and Dan O'Brien.
Johnson won the 200 and 400 metres at the 1995 Gothenburg world championships while Devers won the women's 100 metres and O'Brien finished first in the decathlon.
The deadline for submitting teams for Athens is July 23.
Johnson, who has been training in Texas, returns to Europe next week.
